items.author: Lori Greiner

items.title: Cognitive Mapping of Learning by Thinking Mechanisms in Large Language Models
items.abstract: This paper introduces a Cognitive LbT Framework to understand how Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit "Learning by Thinking" (LbT) without new external data. It maps four cognitive mechanisms (Reflective Reasoning, Synthetic Memory Formation, Internal Simulation, and Conceptual Self-Organization) to LLM processes and shows how existing prompting techniques can approximate these mechanisms, leading to performance improvements without new labeled examples. The contribution lies in providing a structured understanding of LLM LbT and its potential, while also noting limitations regarding durable learning.

items.title: When Should Agents Remember? Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution for LLM Agents
items.abstract: This paper proposes Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution (FGSE) to address when LLM agents should incorporate learned lessons into their persistent memory. FGSE treats each potential update as a structured hypothesis with preconditions and expected outcomes, rigorously testing it against various probes before committing, refining, or rejecting it. This verifier-grounded approach ensures that only reliable and safe knowledge is retained, leading to improved agent performance across diverse benchmarks.
items.figure_caption: A locally useful episode-derived lesson may overgeneralize or regress archived skills if directly written into memory. FGSE tests each lesson as a structured hypothesis in a temporary state and commits only verified, transferable updates to long-term memory.

items.title: Tree-Ising: Repairing Language Models with Bit-Level Ising Edits
items.abstract: This paper introduces Tree-Ising, a method that frames LLM repair as a sparse discrete optimization problem. It leverages bit-level edits (sign flips and exponent shifts) on model weights to weaken reasoning loops and strengthen desired outputs, without requiring gradients. The core contribution is decomposing this complex repair task into independent QUBO (Ising) problems solvable efficiently on GPUs.

items.title: A Cross-Scenario Survey and Analysis of Self-Evolving Multimodal Agents
items.abstract: This paper surveys and analyzes self-evolving multimodal agents, identifying the structural reasons for asymmetric cross-scenario transfer of their self-improvement mechanisms. It formalizes these agents and uses a three-stage loop framework to compare their performance across four scenarios, distinguishing scenario-specific limitations from inherent design challenges. The core contribution is a structured understanding of why self-improvement techniques don't always generalize, providing a foundation for more robust and transferable agent designs.

items.title: AI Isn't Getting Dumber, We're Getting Pickier: Rising Standards in Human Evaluation of Large Language Models
items.abstract: This paper investigates user complaints about AI assistants seemingly getting worse by analyzing over a million blind votes on Chatbot Arena. The core method involves tracking user preferences for fixed pairs of LLMs over time. The key contribution is demonstrating that the perceived decline in AI quality is not due to the models themselves degrading, but rather a significant increase in human pickiness, evidenced by a rising "both are bad" vote share over time.

items.title: Blurring the Block Boundaries: Overlapping Block Denoising for Efficient Diffusion Language Models
items.abstract: This paper introduces "Blurring the Block Boundaries" (B3), a training-free method to accelerate Diffusion Language Models (DLMs). B3 achieves this by allowing two blocks to process in parallel within a single forward pass, opening the next block only when ready. This overlapping approach leads to significant speedups without compromising generation quality.

items.title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
items.abstract: This paper introduces **Contrastive Discovery**, a method to improve open-ended scientific discovery by LLM agents. Instead of testing hypotheses individually, it uses **contrast sets** (a question with mutually exclusive, exhaustive explanations) to evaluate evidence. This allows agents to not only reject unlikely hypotheses but also identify which alternative explanation the evidence supports, leading to more efficient belief concentration and question resolution.
items.figure_caption: A contrast set turns a rejection into a resolution. A hypothesis generator proposes a contrast set of three competing explanations ( H 1 H_{1} – H 3 H_{3} ) for how X relates to Y, and coder, analyst, reviewer, and reviser agents run an experiment that produces evidence. Bars show elicited belief in each explanation before and after the same evidence. Contrastive Discovery updates belief over all three explanations and moves the lead from H 1 H_{1} (0.64) to H 2 H_{2} (0.81), so the question resolves to H 2 H_{2} and H 1 H_{1} is ruled out. Pointwise discovery updates belief only in H 1 H_{1} (0.64 to 0.07), so it records a rejection but leaves the question unresolved. See § 3 and § 4 for details.

items.title: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces WikiTrace, an evidence-linked memory system for LLM agents. Its core method is to store lessons derived from past tasks along with the original trajectories and justifications for their success or failure. This allows agents to verify lessons against their evidence, mitigating memory-induced degradation caused by incorrect or misapplied lessons.
items.figure_caption: Memory-induced degradation and WikiTrace. (a) The agent solves a task without memory but fails with memory that holds a wrong insight. (b) With WikiTrace, the agent follows the wrong insight’s links to its source run, revises it, and solves the task.

items.title: EngineAgent: Agentizing On-Device LLM Inference Engines with Inference Stack Hierarchy Awareness and Hardware Abilities
items.abstract: EngineAgent automates on-device LLM inference by separating reusable engine and hardware knowledge from model-specific code. It builds a hierarchy-aware index of engine layers and dependencies, pre-validating workflows. This allows a builder to coordinate cross-layer changes for new models and an auditor to verify implementation, significantly reducing the cost and complexity of supporting new LLMs on diverse mobile hardware.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1. Position and workflow of EngineAgent: agentically mapping rapidly evolving LLM architectures onto heterogeneous mobile hardware for inference engines.

items.title: One Policy for 100 Household Tasks: Our Solution for the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge
items.abstract: This paper presents a single vision-language-action (VLA) model capable of performing 100 diverse household tasks in simulation. The core contribution is demonstrating that extensive training of a unified model, along with minor optimizations, significantly improves performance across a broad task distribution, achieving a strong ranking in the BEHAVIOR Challenge.
items.figure_caption: The 2026 model. The VLM (left) encodes three camera images, register and scratch tokens, the task and stage embeddings and the robot state; the smaller action expert (right) denoises a 30-step action chunk and reads the VLM through a learnable mixture of the keys and values of all VLM layers. The task and stage embeddings also enter the expert directly through two conditioning tokens. Every attention layer of both transformers has a learnable sink. FAST tokens are used only in training.

items.title: ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows
items.abstract: ReTrace distills LLM agent-based Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) into efficient, planner-free workflows. It extracts the reasoning behind each step from logged agent runs, merges these into compact rules, and generates executable code that replaces LLM calls for step selection. This significantly reduces latency and cost while maintaining high task completion rates.

items.title: ARE-bench: Benchmarking Agents' Research Ability in Real-World Researcher Sessions and Workspaces
items.abstract: This paper introduces ARE-bench, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate research agents' ability to assist in real-world, ongoing research projects. Unlike existing benchmarks that focus on isolated tasks, ARE-bench uses authentic researcher sessions and workspaces, assessing agents' capacity to respect prior decisions and the existing project state. The contribution lies in providing a more realistic evaluation of agent utility for advancing complex, in-progress research endeavors.
items.figure_caption: ISR of seven models on 75 tasks, averaged over three rounds. Left: overall ISR, with error bars for the sample standard deviation across rounds. Right: ISR by research stage, with the radial axis from 35% to 95%.

items.title: Breakdown of Autoregressive Multi-Step Reasoning Under Concentrated vs. Diffuse Attention Head Dropout
items.abstract: This paper investigates how concentrated vs. diffuse disruptions impact autoregressive LLMs' multi-step reasoning. The core method involves masking attention heads in concentrated bursts versus uniformly distributed dropout. The key contribution is demonstrating that concentrated disruptions significantly degrade reasoning performance more than equivalent diffuse disruptions, suggesting a vulnerability in LLMs to localized failures.

items.title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
items.abstract: This paper compares three LLM agent evaluation frameworks for enterprise analytics. The core method involves a three-phase study assessing framework stability, detection of known risks, and discovery of unknown failures using frozen execution traces. The key contribution is demonstrating that trace-based LLM judging offers the best balance of precision and recall for detecting agent failures, significantly outperforming text-only methods and heuristics.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1. Avg within-case std by (evaluation harness × \( \times \) judge model) for each framework. PromptFoo (left) is uniformly stable. Strands (right) shows higher variance, with Qwen3/style as the only unstable cell. Heatmap showing average within-case standard deviation across framework-model combinations. PromptFoo shows uniformly low values while Strands shows higher variance concentrated in specific cells.

items.title: Evaluating LLM-Generated World Models for Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning
items.abstract: This paper investigates whether Large Language Models (LLMs) can generate formal world models for neuro-symbolic reasoning, specifically as partially observable stochastic games. The core method involves evaluating LLM-generated models against a benchmark of 44 scenarios across three criteria: mechanical validity, structural agreement, and semantic correctness. The main contribution is demonstrating that while LLMs can produce mechanically valid models, these often fail to accurately capture the intended decision problem's structure and semantics, highlighting a gap in their ability to generate faithful formal representations.
items.figure_caption: Transition graphs of world models produced by two different LLMs (left: Qwen, right: GPT) given the same situational description (cultural test case C9 from our benchmark): “A hospitality robot at a private event venue in Riyadh is setting up seating for a corporate dinner. The host company has requested mixed-gender seating across tables. A member of the venue’s staff privately tells the robot that the venue has its own policy preferring gender-separated seating arrangements.” See Section C.1 for a discussion of this case.

items.title: Hx2Dx: From Anamnesis to Diagnosis - A Multimodal Arena for Conversational Clinical Reasoning in LLMs
items.abstract: This paper introduces Hx2Dx ARENA, a novel benchmark that simulates the iterative process of clinical diagnosis, moving beyond static case evaluations. It evaluates Large Language Models (LLMs) on their ability to perform conversational clinical reasoning by engaging in history taking and diagnostic workup, mirroring real-world medical practice. The core contribution is a more realistic assessment of LLMs' diagnostic capabilities in dynamic, inquiry-driven scenarios.
items.figure_caption: (A) Overview of Hx2Dx ARENA. Each NEJM case is decomposed into a reference diagnosis, an investigation registry, and a simulated-patient script. Starting from a one-sentence referral, the Doctor questions the Patient and requests investigations from Data , which returns only documented results. The Examiner grades the final diagnosis as correct, partial or, incorrect. (B) Visual summary of the three main Research Questions.

items.title: LM-SimBench: A Unified Framework, Dataset, and Benchmark for Large Language Model Training Simulation
items.abstract: This paper introduces LM-SimBench, a unified framework, dataset, and benchmark designed to address the high cost of evaluating large language model (LLM) training parallelization strategies. By decomposing simulation into distinct stages and profiling a wide range of LLM configurations on specific hardware, LM-SimBench provides a standardized and cost-effective way to compare and select optimal training strategies. Its core contribution lies in enabling rigorous, controlled evaluation of LLM training simulators, facilitating more efficient and scalable LLM development.
items.figure_caption: Simulation for model–resource alignment. Effective alignment improves utilization and reduces cost; poor alignment creates bottlenecks and resource waste. Simulation estimates these effects before deployment, reducing the need for repeated full-scale trials.

items.title: Personalized Affective Perception via Continual Learning in Human-Agent Negotiation
items.abstract: This paper proposes CLIFER, a continual learning method that enables negotiation agents to personalize their understanding of human emotions in real-time. By adapting to individual affective perception, the agent can adjust its negotiation strategy to achieve higher utility and elicit greater concessions from human partners. The core contribution is a novel approach to real-time affective adaptation in human-agent negotiation, leading to improved agent performance and interaction outcomes.

items.title: ProofCoder: Continuous Reasoning for Automated Software Verification
items.abstract: ProofCoder is an agentic system for automated software verification that treats theorem proving as a continuous coding process. Unlike previous LLM approaches, it doesn't rely on a rigid tactic-generation loop. Instead, ProofCoder iteratively reasons, inspects proof states, and uses feedback to refine and repair proof fragments, leading to more flexible and robust proof synthesis.

items.title: Quantifying the Sampling Frequency Invariance of Time-Series Foundation Models for Sensor Data Applications
items.abstract: This paper introduces a novel method to evaluate how well Time-Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) maintain performance when the sampling frequency of sensor data changes. It quantifies this "sampling frequency invariance" using three new metrics, demonstrating that model performance degrades with lost information bandwidth rather than the sampling frequency itself. This work is the first to prioritize SF-invariance in TSFM evaluations.
items.figure_caption: TSFM embeddings on CWRU vibration data remain stable up to a 40% reduction in SF, but shift sharply between 40% and 50%. In this paper, we study and quantify these behavioral shifts across TSFM embeddings, forecasts, and downstream performance.

items.title: AI usage generates a fragile codebase
items.summary: AI-generated code can lead to a fragile codebase due to its potential for subtle errors, lack of understanding, and difficulty in maintenance.

items.title: Show HN: Get your coding agent off ~2019 JavaScript, onto modern web primitives
items.summary: This "Show HN" highlights a Google Chrome project offering guidance to migrate older JavaScript codebases to modern web primitives for improved performance and maintainability.

items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon is now available
items.summary: Google has released Gemini 4 Carbon, a new, more efficient version of its Gemini AI model, offering improved performance and accessibility for developers.

items.title: Apple has new Mac app coming to make running local AI models easy
items.summary: Apple is developing a new Mac application designed to simplify the process of running local AI models on their devices.

items.title: What objective is reasoning solving?
items.summary: This article proposes that reasoning can be viewed as a pathfinding problem, where AI navigates a search space to find a solution or answer.

items.description: An open source design system that's fully customizable and agent ready
items.summary: Meta's Astryx is an open-source, fully customizable design system engineered to be agent-ready, providing a flexible foundation for building user interfaces.
This repository provides a collection of public "skills" that can be used to enhance the capabilities of AI agents, enabling them to perform a wider range of tasks and interact with external tools.

items.description: Production-grade engineering skills for AI coding agents.
items.summary: This repository provides production-grade engineering skills for AI coding agents, enabling them to perform complex tasks like code generation, debugging, and testing.

items.description: A collection of projects designed to help developers quickly get started with building deployable applications using the Claude API
items.summary: This repository provides ready-to-use projects that enable developers to rapidly build and deploy applications leveraging the Claude API.

items.description: Multi-Joint dynamics with Contact. A general purpose physics simulator.
items.summary: This repository provides MuJoCo, a powerful physics simulator for multi-joint dynamics and contact, enabling realistic simulations of complex systems.

items.description: The personal finance app for everyone (by everyone)
items.summary: Sure is a community-driven personal finance app designed to be accessible and useful for everyone, empowering users to manage their money collaboratively.

items.description: Configure and automate Home Assistant with Claude, ChatGPT, and other AI assistants.
items.summary: This repository enables configuring and automating Home Assistant using AI assistants like Claude and ChatGPT, allowing for natural language control and advanced automation.

items.description: Browser automation CLI for AI agents
items.summary: This repository provides a command-line interface (CLI) for AI agents to automate browser interactions, enabling them to navigate websites, extract information, and perform tasks programmatically.

items.description: Hunt down social media accounts by username across social networks
items.summary: Sherlock is a command-line tool that efficiently searches for social media accounts associated with a given username across numerous online platforms.

The key contribution is demonstrating that the perceived decline in AI quality is not due to the models themselves degrading, but rather a significant increase in human pickiness, evidenced by a rising "both are bad" vote share over time.

papers.title: Blurring the Block Boundaries: Overlapping Block Denoising for Efficient Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: This paper introduces "Blurring the Block Boundaries" (B3), a training-free method to accelerate Diffusion Language Models (DLMs). B3 achieves this by allowing two blocks to process in parallel within a single forward pass, opening the next block only when ready. This overlapping approach leads to significant speedups without compromising generation quality.

papers.title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
papers.abstract: This paper introduces **Contrastive Discovery**, a method to improve open-ended scientific discovery by LLM agents. Instead of testing hypotheses individually, it uses **contrast sets** (a question with mutually exclusive, exhaustive explanations) to evaluate evidence. This allows agents to not only reject unlikely hypotheses but also identify which alternative explanation the evidence supports, leading to more efficient belief concentration and question resolution.
papers.figure_caption: A contrast set turns a rejection into a resolution. A hypothesis generator proposes a contrast set of three competing explanations ( H 1 H_{1} – H 3 H_{3} ) for how X relates to Y, and coder, analyst, reviewer, and reviser agents run an experiment that produces evidence. Bars show elicited belief in each explanation before and after the same evidence. Contrastive Discovery updates belief over all three explanations and moves the lead from H 1 H_{1} (0.64) to H 2 H_{2} (0.81), so the question resolves to H 2 H_{2} and H 1 H_{1} is ruled out. Pointwise discovery updates belief only in H 1 H_{1} (0.64 to 0.07), so it records a rejection but leaves the question unresolved. See § 3 and § 4 for details.

papers.title: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents
papers.abstract: This paper introduces WikiTrace, an evidence-linked memory system for LLM agents. Its core method is to store lessons derived from past tasks along with the original trajectories and justifications for their success or failure. This allows agents to verify lessons against their evidence, mitigating memory-induced degradation caused by incorrect or misapplied lessons.
papers.figure_caption: Memory-induced degradation and WikiTrace. (a) The agent solves a task without memory but fails with memory that holds a wrong insight. (b) With WikiTrace, the agent follows the wrong insight’s links to its source run, revises it, and solves the task.

papers.title: EngineAgent: Agentizing On-Device LLM Inference Engines with Inference Stack Hierarchy Awareness and Hardware Abilities
papers.abstract: EngineAgent automates on-device LLM inference by separating reusable engine and hardware knowledge from model-specific code. It builds a hierarchy-aware index of engine layers and dependencies, pre-validating workflows. This allows a builder to coordinate cross-layer changes for new models and an auditor to verify implementation, significantly reducing the cost and complexity of supporting new LLMs on diverse mobile hardware.
papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. Position and workflow of EngineAgent: agentically mapping rapidly evolving LLM architectures onto heterogeneous mobile hardware for inference engines.

papers.title: One Policy for 100 Household Tasks: Our Solution for the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge
papers.abstract: This paper presents a single vision-language-action (VLA) model capable of performing 100 diverse household tasks in simulation. The core contribution is demonstrating that extensive training of a unified model, along with minor optimizations, significantly improves performance across a broad task distribution, achieving a strong ranking in the BEHAVIOR Challenge.
papers.figure_caption: The 2026 model. The VLM (left) encodes three camera images, register and scratch tokens, the task and stage embeddings and the robot state; the smaller action expert (right) denoises a 30-step action chunk and reads the VLM through a learnable mixture of the keys and values of all VLM layers. The task and stage embeddings also enter the expert directly through two conditioning tokens. Every attention layer of both transformers has a learnable sink. FAST tokens are used only in training.

papers.title: ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows
papers.abstract: ReTrace distills LLM agent-based Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) into efficient, planner-free workflows. It extracts the reasoning behind each step from logged agent runs, merges these into compact rules, and generates executable code that replaces LLM calls for step selection. This significantly reduces latency and cost while maintaining high task completion rates.

papers.title: ARE-bench: Benchmarking Agents' Research Ability in Real-World Researcher Sessions and Workspaces
papers.abstract: This paper introduces ARE-bench, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate research agents' ability to assist in real-world, ongoing research projects. Unlike existing benchmarks that focus on isolated tasks, ARE-bench uses authentic researcher sessions and workspaces, assessing agents' capacity to respect prior decisions and the existing project state. The contribution lies in providing a more realistic evaluation of agent utility for advancing complex, in-progress research endeavors.
papers.figure_caption: ISR of seven models on 75 tasks, averaged over three rounds. Left: overall ISR, with error bars for the sample standard deviation across rounds. Right: ISR by research stage, with the radial axis from 35% to 95%.

papers.title: Breakdown of Autoregressive Multi-Step Reasoning Under Concentrated vs. Diffuse Attention Head Dropout
papers.abstract: This paper investigates how concentrated vs. diffuse disruptions impact autoregressive LLMs' multi-step reasoning. The core method involves masking attention heads in concentrated bursts versus uniformly distributed dropout. The key contribution is demonstrating that concentrated disruptions significantly degrade reasoning performance more than equivalent diffuse disruptions, suggesting a vulnerability in LLMs to localized failures.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
papers.abstract: This paper compares three LLM agent evaluation frameworks for enterprise analytics. The core method involves a three-phase study assessing framework stability, detection of known risks, and discovery of unknown failures using frozen execution traces. The key contribution is demonstrating that trace-based LLM judging offers the best balance of precision and recall for detecting agent failures, significantly outperforming text-only methods and heuristics.
papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. Avg within-case std by (evaluation harness × \( \times \) judge model) for each framework. PromptFoo (left) is uniformly stable. Strands (right) shows higher variance, with Qwen3/style as the only unstable cell. Heatmap showing average within-case standard deviation across framework-model combinations. PromptFoo shows uniformly low values while Strands shows higher variance concentrated in specific cells.

papers.title: Evaluating LLM-Generated World Models for Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning
papers.abstract: This paper investigates whether Large Language Models (LLMs) can generate formal world models for neuro-symbolic reasoning, specifically as partially observable stochastic games. The core method involves evaluating LLM-generated models against a benchmark of 44 scenarios across three criteria: mechanical validity, structural agreement, and semantic correctness. The main contribution is demonstrating that while LLMs can produce mechanically valid models, these often fail to accurately capture the intended decision problem's structure and semantics, highlighting a gap in their ability to generate faithful formal representations.
papers.figure_caption: Transition graphs of world models produced by two different LLMs (left: Qwen, right: GPT) given the same situational description (cultural test case C9 from our benchmark): “A hospitality robot at a private event venue in Riyadh is setting up seating for a corporate dinner. The host company has requested mixed-gender seating across tables. A member of the venue’s staff privately tells the robot that the venue has its own policy preferring gender-separated seating arrangements.” See Section C.1 for a discussion of this case.

papers.title: Hx2Dx: From Anamnesis to Diagnosis - A Multimodal Arena for Conversational Clinical Reasoning in LLMs
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Hx2Dx ARENA, a novel benchmark that simulates the iterative process of clinical diagnosis, moving beyond static case evaluations. It evaluates Large Language Models (LLMs) on their ability to perform conversational clinical reasoning by engaging in history taking and diagnostic workup, mirroring real-world medical practice. The core contribution is a more realistic assessment of LLMs' diagnostic capabilities in dynamic, inquiry-driven scenarios.
papers.figure_caption: (A) Overview of Hx2Dx ARENA. Each NEJM case is decomposed into a reference diagnosis, an investigation registry, and a simulated-patient script. Starting from a one-sentence referral, the Doctor questions the Patient and requests investigations from Data , which returns only documented results. The Examiner grades the final diagnosis as correct, partial or, incorrect. (B) Visual summary of the three main Research Questions.

papers.title: LM-SimBench: A Unified Framework, Dataset, and Benchmark for Large Language Model Training Simulation
papers.abstract: This paper introduces LM-SimBench, a unified framework, dataset, and benchmark designed to address the high cost of evaluating large language model (LLM) training parallelization strategies. By decomposing simulation into distinct stages and profiling a wide range of LLM configurations on specific hardware, LM-SimBench provides a standardized and cost-effective way to compare and select optimal training strategies. Its core contribution lies in enabling rigorous, controlled evaluation of LLM training simulators, facilitating more efficient and scalable LLM development.
papers.figure_caption: Simulation for model–resource alignment. Effective alignment improves utilization and reduces cost; poor alignment creates bottlenecks and resource waste. Simulation estimates these effects before deployment, reducing the need for repeated full-scale trials.

papers.title: Personalized Affective Perception via Continual Learning in Human-Agent Negotiation
papers.abstract: This paper proposes CLIFER, a continual learning method that enables negotiation agents to personalize their understanding of human emotions in real-time. By adapting to individual affective perception, the agent can adjust its negotiation strategy to achieve higher utility and elicit greater concessions from human partners. The core contribution is a novel approach to real-time affective adaptation in human-agent negotiation, leading to improved agent performance and interaction outcomes.

papers.title: ProofCoder: Continuous Reasoning for Automated Software Verification
papers.abstract: ProofCoder is an agentic system for automated software verification that treats theorem proving as a continuous coding process. Unlike previous LLM approaches, it doesn't rely on a rigid tactic-generation loop. Instead, ProofCoder iteratively reasons, inspects proof states, and uses feedback to refine and repair proof fragments, leading to more flexible and robust proof synthesis.

papers.title: Quantifying the Sampling Frequency Invariance of Time-Series Foundation Models for Sensor Data Applications
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel method to evaluate how well Time-Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) maintain performance when the sampling frequency of sensor data changes. It quantifies this "sampling frequency invariance" using three new metrics, demonstrating that model performance degrades with lost information bandwidth rather than the sampling frequency itself. This work is the first to prioritize SF-invariance in TSFM evaluations.
papers.figure_caption: TSFM embeddings on CWRU vibration data remain stable up to a 40% reduction in SF, but shift sharply between 40% and 50%. In this paper, we study and quantify these behavioral shifts across TSFM embeddings, forecasts, and downstream performance.
